title: Panel membership visible in the scenario trace (#3 prefactor)
description:
Make the Panel's membership visible in the scenario trace, so the Conformance Suite can see a
Reviewer that was never spawned. Pure prefactor for #3: no requirement changes, the suite stays
green, and the enumeration does not grow.

## Why

`observed_trace()` in `conformance/run` (lines 46–68) reconstructs `panel<r>:<class>` by counting
only the Reviewers that recorded a run, so three-spawned-three-ok renders as `panel<r>:all`,
byte-identical to four. The formal side has the same hole: `tools/formal/Rloop/Loop.lean:95`
makes the Panel a single `Spawn` constructor carrying a `Panel` class, and `Scenarios.lean:74`
renders it `s!"panel{r}:{panelName p}"` — there is nowhere to record *which* Reviewers ran.

**All 206 committed scenarios would stay green over an Implementation that silently ran three
Reviewers.** Same class as the CodeRabbit finding on #2.

This contradicts #3's settled comment, which said the Lean model needs no change. That is true of
the decision function and wrong about the trace, where the Suite's coverage actually lives — see
the correction comment on #3 (2026-09-20T21:28:04Z). `tools/formal/` is in scope.

## What to change

- `Spawn.panel` carries the membership.
- The render in `Scenarios.lean` emits it.
- `python3 tools/check_scenarios.py --write` rewrites all 206 rows with the longer trace token;
  commit what it writes (`AGENTS.md`: the scenarios file is rendered, not hand-kept).
- `observed_trace()` in `conformance/run` is taught to match.

## Why it does not grow the enumeration

Under today's requirements every Panel is the same four Reviewers, so membership is a constant.
The alphabet is unchanged; only the token is longer. Availability as an *axis* is a different
job and belongs with the requirement change — see the availability-scenario-axis ticket.

## Acceptance

- `nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh` exits 0, unpiped, all six gates PASS.
- `conformance/scenarios.tsv` still has 206 rows, each with membership in the trace column.
- A fake scripted to skip one Reviewer **fails** a scenario that expects four. It does not today;
  that failure is the whole point of this ticket and must be demonstrated, not asserted.
- No requirement text changes. `git diff` touches only `tools/formal/`, `tools/`-written files
  and `conformance/`.

## Lands next to

`F4` ("The scenario alphabet is a choice"), whose closing line now has a sibling case: an
Implementation that passes the suite while running a three-Reviewer Panel.

title: Specify the model-availability probe and the fail-open rule (#3)
description:
Specify the model-availability probe: its command lines, when it runs, and the fail-open rule.
The first half of #3. Nothing changes about what rloop does with the answer — that is the
record-omitted-reviewer ticket.

## Why

An exhausted model does not fail fast. It hangs, writes zero bytes on both streams, and is killed
at its seat's timeout. A Reviewer seat pays `--reviewer-timeout` (1800s default) **every Round**
for a model that was never going to answer.

Verified 2026-09-20: `claude -p "/usage"` exits 0 in seconds and reports per-family limits with
reset times, and answers just as fast *through* the exhausted model, so one call covers every
claude family. codex exposes no quota at all; both codex seats share one ChatGPT account, so a
tiny `codex exec` call is the only direct probe and one probe covers both.

## Settled already (#3, do not re-derive)

- **The check runs immediately before the Panel, never at Run start.** `astra` and `sol` produced
  the same counterexample independently: an Implementer call may run for hours past a quota reset,
  so evidence gathered at Run start can suppress a Reviewer that would have answered.
- **Fail open.** Unknown availability, a probe that fails, output that does not parse, or an
  unrecognised model name MUST spawn the Reviewer normally. Only positively recognised, unexpired
  exhaustion may short-circuit.
- **Remove only, never substitute.** Substitution silently changes which model judged the work.
- **The parser lives in this Specification.** The "language-neutral" objection is answered in #3
  point 7: this set is language-neutral about the *Implementation* (`ADR-0001`) and is
  deliberately harness-specific everywhere else — it already hardcodes the model names, the
  `--effort` values and the deny list byte for byte, and `AGT-17` pins the CLI versions.

## What to change

- A new requirement for the probe's command lines, stated verbatim like every other
  (`ADR-0001`, `OVR-2`), with `tools/check_fixtures.py --write` regenerating the fixtures. Never
  edit `conformance/fixtures/` by hand.
- **Narrow `OVR-1`**, which forbids the probe as written: *"It MUST NOT parse a Reviewer's
  output, an Implementer's output, or any part of the Finished File beyond its first line."* A
  quota probe is rloop parsing a model CLI's output and acting on it. Follow `F9`'s six-day-old
  precedent exactly: it narrowed `DIR-4`'s "entire and *unparsed*" to "entire and *unmodified*"
  to admit one datum. This is the second instance of that pattern.
- `AGT-17`: record the CLI versions the `/usage` format was verified against. `AGT-17` already
  concedes this risk class — *"a flag that a newer CLI rejects is found only by a live Run"* — so
  a drifted format is not a new kind of exposure, and fail-open degrades it to doing nothing.
- `CNF` items in `06-conformance.md` for the three fail-open paths: probe fails, probe output
  does not parse, unrecognised model name. Distinguish exhaustion from a typo: verified,
  `claude -p "say hi" --model claude-bogus-9` exits 1 in seconds with
  `[claude-code:unrecognized_model]`, while exhaustion hangs with zero bytes.

## ADR

**`ADR-0006`**, not `ADR-0005`. #3's settled comment reserved 0005, and 0005 was taken on
2026-09-21 by "The operator's view has one home and Implementations point at it". Check
`docs/adr/` for the next free number before writing, not this ticket.

Subject: rloop reads a vendor's human-facing quota report and fails open. Hard to reverse,
surprising without context, and argued against by all three advisers — record what they said and
why it was overridden.

## Acceptance

- `nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh` exits 0, unpiped, all six gates PASS.
- `grep` finds the probe's command line in exactly one document, and its fixture is generated.
- Every new requirement is cited by a `CNF` item. The coverage gate holds at zero with no ratchet
  baseline, so an excuse-table entry is not available here — and would be false, since #3's
  Testability section says all of this is black-box testable.

title: Record an unavailable Reviewer in place, never drop it (#3)
description:
An unavailable Reviewer stays in the Panel and is recorded as not having run, rather than being
dropped so the Panel runs with three. The second half of #3, and the part that changes behaviour.

Depends on the availability-probe ticket: fail-open means unknown availability MUST spawn
normally, so without a probe command line this arm is unreachable in a live Run and unscriptable
in the Suite — there is nothing for a fake to answer.

## Settled already (#3, do not re-derive)

- **Record, do not drop.** Consequence: there is no Panel floor to choose. `RUN-15` already fixes
  one — one survivor is enough, zero is exit 2 — and no version of this change alters it.
  Question 1 of #3 is withdrawn.
- **"Did not run" counts toward `RUN-15`'s zero-survivor abort.** An account wholly out of quota
  therefore loses the Round: the Implementer may have run for hours and committed work, and rloop
  exits 2 with no judge and no Finished File. Accepted unchanged — four timeouts reach the
  identical exit today, two hours later, and `F10` already rejected having rloop author a
  `finished.md` of its own for precisely this case.
- **A distinct literal is required.** `REVIEWER FAILED (exit <status>)` cannot describe a call
  that never happened — there is no status — and `PRM-2` tells the Manager that line means
  `crashed or timed out`. Reusing it makes both passages false and costs the Manager the
  distinction `RUN-15`'s own rationale rests on: *"One Reviewer down is a degraded Panel the
  Manager can weigh; four down is a broken environment."*
- **No new noun.** A `Seat`/occupant split was proposed and withdrawn by its own proposer.

## What to change

- `RUN-15`: a third arm for the omitted call, and which failures count toward the abort.
- `RUN-7` §3 — *"all four Reviewer calls … started concurrently and all waited for"* — goes
  false. Amend it.
- `RUN-8`.
- `PRM-2`: the distinct literal. Amended either way, per the settled comment.
- `DIR-4`: the Feedback File's authorship when rloop writes it in the Reviewer's place, and an
  absent or empty `.err`.
- `CONTEXT.md`: the two glossary entries drafted in #3 land **here**, not earlier — the Feedback
  File entry cites a `RUN-15` clause that does not exist until this ticket.

  ```
  **Panel**:
  The **Reviewers** `AGT-11` designates for one **Round**, each a different model, run side by
  side.

  **Feedback File**:
  One **Reviewer**'s findings for one **Round**, written for the **Manager**; rloop writes it in
  the Reviewer's place when the call failed or was never made (`RUN-15`).
  _Avoid_: Review, findings file
  ```

- `PRM-4` does **not** change. `PRM-6` forbids conditional text, and "one of four independent
  Reviewers" stays true of a designated roster.

## Acceptance

- `nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh` exits 0, unpiped, all six gates PASS.
- All four unavailable exits 2 with no judge spawned and no Finished File — **instantly**, not
  after four timeouts. This is `RUN-15`'s existing rule firing on the new arm, not separate
  behaviour, which is why it has no ticket of its own.
- The Manager can tell "did not run" from "crashed or timed out" by reading the Feedback File
  alone. Grep `PRM-2` for both literals.
- Before writing that a clause landed, `grep` for its identifier. A decision gets its identifier
  when it is accepted (`AGENTS.md`).

title: Availability as a scenario axis: the six cases (#3)
description:
Add availability as an axis in the scenario alphabet and generate the six cases #3 requires
before any of this is trusted. This is the ticket that grows the enumeration.

Depends on the panel-membership-in-trace ticket (the trace needs somewhere to put membership) and
on the record-omitted-reviewer ticket (the behaviour has to exist to be enumerated).

## Why separate from the prefactor

Making membership visible does not grow the alphabet: under today's requirements every Panel is
the same four Reviewers, so membership is a constant. Enumerating *availability* multiplies the
generated set, so it belongs with the requirement change rather than with the mechanical
rewrite. Splitting them keeps a 206-row regeneration reviewable on its own.

## The six cases, from #3

1. One Reviewer unavailable — recorded, not spawned; the Run continues with the rest.
2. All four unavailable — exit 2, no judge spawned, no Finished File.
3. A Reviewer re-admitted in a later Round, once the fake reports capacity again.
4. A probe that fails — fail open, the Reviewer is spawned.
5. A probe whose output does not parse — fail open, the Reviewer is spawned.
6. An unrecognised model name — fail open and loud, not a silently smaller Panel.

Cases 4–6 are the fail-open paths. They are the ones that make the rule falsifiable; without
them "fail open" is a sentence nobody can check.

## What to change

- Availability as an axis in `tools/formal/Rloop/Scenarios.lean`'s alphabet.
- `python3 tools/check_scenarios.py --write`, then commit what it writes.
- The fakes in `conformance/` gain a way to report exhaustion and to report capacity again.
- `conformance/scenarios.tsv`.

## Acceptance

- `nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh` exits 0, unpiped, all six gates PASS.
- Each of the six cases fails against an Implementation that gets it wrong. Demonstrate the
  failure for each; a scenario that passes both ways tests nothing. This is the lesson `F5`
  already paid for — *"a check and its subject built from one misreading agree with each other"*.
- The row count grows, and the growth is reported in the commit message with the before and
  after.

## Lands next to

`F4` ("The scenario alphabet is a choice"). If this materially multiplies the set, say so in
`F4` — it is the finding that owns the size of the enumeration.

title: PRM-4's clean-path shortcut swallows item 0 (#4)
description:
`PRM-4`'s report block contradicts itself on the clean path, and the contradiction is why a codex
Reviewer's bare `No findings.` carries no provenance. Fix the prompt; no vendor reasoning needed.

## The defect

Item 0 says *"Say 'I ran everything I needed' if that is true"*. The block then ends:

```
If there is nothing to report, write exactly: No findings.
```

`write exactly` names a literal, and it is the last and most specific instruction in the block. A
Reviewer with nothing to report is being told to emit that string and nothing else. The codex
Reviewers comply; `opus` is the one deviating by adding item 0 on top.

Evidence is on rloop-spec#4 (2026-09-21 comment): across seven Run Directories every bare report
is **exactly 13 bytes**, and every codex Reviewer that was itself blocked wrote item 0 in full —
including `sol`, which #4's original text reports as never complying.

## The change

In `03-prompts.md`, `PRM-4`, replace the closing line of the report block with:

```
If you have nothing for items 1 and 2, write item 0 and then exactly: No findings.
```

Keeps the literal that makes a clean report machine-recognisable; stops it swallowing item 0.

Then `python3 tools/check_fixtures.py --write`. Never edit `conformance/fixtures/` by hand
(`AGENTS.md`). A prompt is changed in `03-prompts.md` and nowhere else.

## What follows in the Implementation

`PRM-4`'s bytes are normative (`OVR-2`), so `rloop-bash` changes its hardcoded prompt and bumps
its `spec/` pin, then `spec/conformance/run ./result/bin/rloop` must pass. That is `ADR-0001`'s
designed path, not an accident of it. `CNF-11`/`CNF-12` compare the hardcoded prompt to the
fixtures byte for byte, so a missed byte fails the suite rather than going live.

## What does not change

`conformance/run` lines 164 and 320 compare a Feedback File to `"No findings."` exactly, but those
are **fake** Reviewers' canned outputs testing rloop's pass-through plumbing. A fake does not read
a prompt. Leave them.

## Acceptance

- `nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh` exits 0, unpiped, all six gates PASS.
- `grep -n "No findings" 03-prompts.md` shows the literal in exactly one place, inside the new
  sentence.
- The regenerated fixture for `PRM-4` matches the document; `check_fixtures.py` proves it.
- In `rloop-bash`: `spec/conformance/run ./result/bin/rloop` passes against the bumped pin.

## Verification is a live observation, not a suite item

Only a live Run shows whether the reworded block is followed — the Suite proves the prompt was
*sent*, never that a model obeyed it (`00-overview.md`, *How much to trust this*). Record it as a
`CNF-22` observation with the next release, against a specific prediction: **a clean codex report
carries item 0 and the literal both.** If it still emits 13 bytes, the cause was not the shortcut
and #4's option 2 — telling the Manager in `PRM-2` to weigh a report with no item 0 — is next.
